solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Drive is what oversleeping worker might do

definitions.meaning: drive in the sense of energy and ambition, a noun

definitions.note: a phrase describing an action, read as the words get up and go
definitions.meaning: someone late for work leaps out of bed and dashes off

explanation.surface: A comment on a worker who has overslept and must rush to the office.
explanation.walkthrough: The same string of words works twice: as a hyphenated noun for energy, and literally as the two actions of a late riser.
explanation.definitionFit: Get-up-and-go is an informal noun for energy and enthusiasm, the quality called drive.

clue.text: God's attitude essentially mortified fellow

parts.note: a pose is an attitude struck, as by a model

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so only the central letter of 'mortified' is wanted

parts.note: the middle of a nine-letter word
a don is a university fellow

explanation.surface: A fellow is embarrassed by a god's haughty attitude.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'God' is read as 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Poseidon is the Greek deity ruling the sea, brother of Zeus.

clue.text: I like company, having over fellow failure

parts.note: f is the standard abbreviation for fellow
used as it stands
as = like, in 'as a child' / 'like a child'
Co is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A sociable person admits to liking company but ends up a lonely failure.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'having over' means the fellow is placed above the rest, so it leads. The surface suggests someone gregarious; each word is just a small abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiasco is a humiliating, complete disaster, so a total flop or failure.

clue.text: Drug stopping one in a relationship conceiving

indicators.note: to stop a hole is to plug it, so the drug sits inside the relationship phrase

parts.note: one as the Roman numeral
going out with someone
E is ecstasy, the usual drug in crosswords

explanation.surface: A drug gets in the way of someone in a couple trying for a baby.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'conceiving' about pregnancy; it means having ideas. E goes into I DATING after the D.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideating means forming ideas or mental images, which is conceiving in its mental sense.

clue.text: US refuse worker entry to abnormally quiet island

indicators.note: the entry to a word is its doorway, its opening letter, taken from 'abnormally'

parts.note: the first letter
sh! is a call for quiet
the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: An American garbage collector gains entry to a strangely silent island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entry' pretends to be about arriving on the island; it only picks a letter. The Isle of Man lies between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage an ashman collected ashes and household rubbish, a garbage collector.

clue.text: Litre in drink must be knocked back? Good point!

indicators.note: a drink knocked back is downed, but here the letters are sent backwards, and in a down clue that means upwards
the litre goes inside the word for drink

parts.note: to sup is to drink
l is the abbreviation for litre

explanation.surface: Someone agrees that a litre of drink should be downed in one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' looks like part of the drinking picture; it turns SULP round.
explanation.definitionFit: A plus is an advantage or favourable feature, a good point in a list of pros and cons.

clue.text: Leading man appearing in The Rocketeer

indicators.note: the answer appears within the film title's letters, spanning two words

parts.note: tHE ROcketeer

explanation.surface: A note about who stars in the film The Rocketeer.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits right beside a film title, so the lead actor's role is lurking in plain sight across two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The hero of a film or story is its principal male character, the lead actor's role.

clue.text: Repurpose my old items in a fresh way?

indicators.note: to repurpose things is to put them to a different use, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder, ten letters

explanation.surface: Upcycling advice: give your old things a new lease of life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' looks like 'new', as the recycling picture wants; it means cheeky or forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh can mean impudent or overly forward, and acting that way is behaving without modesty.

clue.text: Experienced chap damn fool threw off

indicators.note: something off is wrong or out of order, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: anagram fodder, thirteen letters

explanation.surface: An old hand says some idiot threw something off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chap' tempts the solver to write MAN as a separate piece; it belongs to the definition, and the fodder supplies MAN itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A man of the world is a worldly, sophisticated fellow who has seen a lot of life.

clue.text: Successful doc finally stops folk smoking

parts.note: a doctor who succeeds heals the patient

indicators.note: finally points to the end of 'stops', its closing letter only

parts.note: the last letter

explanation.surface: A doctor finally gets his patients to give up cigarettes.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes smoking a habit to kick; here it is the smoking of fish or ham to preserve it.
explanation.definitionFit: Curers preserve meat or fish by salting or drying, and smoking is one method of curing.

clue.text: Miserly teacher getting a close shave

parts.note: near is an old word for stingy
Miss is how pupils address a female teacher

explanation.surface: A stingy teacher skimps on a razor and nearly cuts himself.
explanation.walkthrough: Near for stingy is dated British usage, now mostly met in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A near miss is a narrow escape from disaster, which a close shave describes idiomatically.

clue.text: Don't touch fruity bunches on holiday

parts.note: a hand is a bunch of bananas
off work, as in 'I'm off next week'

explanation.surface: A warning not to touch the fruit bought on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: A hand of bananas is the grocer's word for a cluster of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Hands off is an exclamation warning someone not to interfere with or grab something.

clue.text: Light tipless fag with dope inside at last

indicators.note: a cigarette without its tip loses its front end, so the word for fag drops its first letter

parts.note: cig, a cigarette, without its opening C
a dope is an idiot, a nit

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of 'inside' only

parts.note: the last letter

explanation.surface: Someone lights a roll-up with drugs packed inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' and 'inside' paint a spliff, but dope is a fool and 'inside at last' supplies one letter. Fag is British slang for a cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: To light a fire or fuse is to set it burning, the same as to ignite it.

clue.text: Religious student hogs toilet getting changed

indicators.note: something changed is altered, so the letters take a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder, ten letters

explanation.surface: A divinity student monopolises the loo while changing clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting changed' reads as dressing in the toilet, but it rearranges the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A theologist studies the nature of God and religious belief, a scholar of divinity.

clue.text: Canine welfare service?

parts.note: surface reading: a charity or vet looking after dogs
setter's reading: a canine is also a pointed tooth, whose welfare is looked after by cleaning

explanation.surface: An animal charity that looks after the wellbeing of dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is 'canine' as a noun for a tooth rather than an adjective for dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: Brushing and flossing care for the teeth, including the pointed ones next to the incisors.

clue.text: Accomplished criminal tainted by Mafia ultimately

indicators.note: a criminal version of something is crooked, so the letters are bent out of order

parts.note: anagram fodder

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the closing letter of 'Mafia' is used

parts.note: the last letter

explanation.surface: A skilled crook is corrupted by the Mob in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accomplished criminal' reads as one phrase, but 'Accomplished' is the definition and 'criminal' the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To attain a goal is to achieve or reach it, so attained is a past-tense synonym.

clue.text: Old brute with black eyes delivered in stretcher?

parts.note: ex = former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: a speech is delivered, so the words are to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: a panda is a big bear with black patches round its eyes

explanation.surface: An old thug with two black eyes is carried off on a stretcher.
explanation.walkthrough: In a British accent that drops the final r, 'ex-panda' and the answer are said alike. The stretcher is a device, not a medical one.
explanation.definitionFit: A chest expander is exercise equipment with springs that you pull apart, stretching them.

clue.text: Beastly type with club stealing medal

indicators.note: a thief takes something in, so the clue words hold the medal inside them

parts.note: w is the abbreviation for with
the Order of Merit, a British honour
a bat is a club, in cricket or baseball

explanation.surface: A thug armed with a club makes off with someone's medal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beastly type' sounds like a brute, but it means a type of beast. The Order of Merit is an honour given by the British monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The wombat is a burrowing Australian marsupial, one kind of animal.

clue.text: Bishop wanting relations to get a stiff drink

parts.note: b is bishop in chess notation
randy = lustful, eager for sex

explanation.surface: A lonely bishop who misses his family reaches for the bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relations' suggests family; it means sexual relations. Randy is British slang for feeling lustful.
explanation.definitionFit: Brandy is a strong spirit distilled from wine, the classic stiff drink for shock.

clue.text: Tree in, say, Red China close to mausoleum

parts.note: red is an example of wine, flagged by 'say'
china = mate, from Cockney rhyming slang china plate

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only the last letter of 'mausoleum' is taken

parts.note: the last letter

explanation.surface: A tree stands near Mao's mausoleum in Communist China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red China' conjures Mao's state, but the capitals hide two separate pieces: a wine and a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine palm is any palm whose sap is tapped and fermented into palm wine, a kind of tree.

clue.text: Foolish to go in numbers to see Wanderers

indicators.note: the word for foolish is told to go inside the abbreviation for numbers

parts.note: nos is short for numbers
mad = crazy, foolish

explanation.surface: Fans are foolish to turn up in large numbers to watch Wanderers play.
explanation.walkthrough: Wanderers is a football club nickname (Bolton, Wolves), which the capital supports; here it means people who roam.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomads are people with no fixed home who travel from place to place.

clue.text: Supercilious old royalist

definitions.note: a noun, where the first definition is an adjective
definitions.meaning: a supporter of Charles I in the English Civil War

explanation.walkthrough: The Cavaliers fought for the king against Cromwell's Roundheads in the 1640s.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavalier attitude is haughtily careless; the historic Cavaliers were King Charles's party.

clue.text: A custom in another country, perhaps

parts.note: used as it stands
a habit or practice, as in 'set in one's ...s'

explanation.surface: A tradition peculiar to some foreign land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks the definition as one example: you can be away without leaving the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Being away means absent from home, and abroad is one instance of that.

clue.text: Bloke with a gun espied at the front? Run!

parts.note: a bloke is a man
used as it stands

indicators.note: the front of each word is its opening, so just the heads of 'gun' and 'espied' are kept

parts.note: the first letters of both words

explanation.surface: Someone spots an armed man up ahead and yells at everyone to flee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run!' is the cry of alarm in the surface; as the definition it is the verb meaning to be in charge of.
explanation.definitionFit: To run a business or project is to manage it, be in charge of its operation.

clue.text: Dad restyled with blade? He's saving on haircuts!

definitions.text: Dad restyled with blade? He's saving on haircuts!

indicators.note: restyling hair arranges it differently, so these letters are arranged differently too

parts.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder
anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A father has his head shaved with a razor, and jokes about the money he'll save.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and a description: a dad shaved to the scalp never pays a barber.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with no hair on top has nothing for a barber to cut, so pays nothing.

clue.text: Flirt taking top off provides relaxation

indicators.note: the top of an across word is its start, so the flirt word loses its first letter

parts.note: tease without its first letter

explanation.surface: A flirt takes her top off to help someone unwind.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at undressing; 'top' is only the first letter of TEASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ease is a state of comfort free from strain, which relaxation also describes.
